skill.name: fix-my-twitter-profile
skill.description: Go through name, bio and pinned tweet in the order a visitor reads them, and fix whichever one is losing the follow. Use when someone asks for a profile review, has a new role or a new offer, says people visit and do not follow, or wants their bio rewritten. Do not stuff keywords, do not promise followers, and do not rewrite the parts that are already working.
skill.summary: Review your Twitter name, bio, pinned tweet, and profile images while preserving the parts that already work.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.value_statement: A vague Twitter profile can leave visitors unsure why they should follow you. This skill reviews your profile and suggests focused changes that match your posts.
actual_capabilities: Adapt profile recommendations to visitors arriving from tweets, replies, search, or recommendations.
Suggest a short name-field description that explains what you post about.
Review and rewrite a bio around what someone gains by following you.
Assess whether a pinned tweet represents your current writing and topics.
Evaluate avatar and header readability at timeline and mobile sizes, and identify profile elements worth keeping.
Use connected VoiceMOAT tools for voice insights and rewritten bio consistency checks when available.
limitations: Does not promise follower growth or generate profile visits.
Requires supplied profile details or accessible profile content for specific recommendations.
Does not provide automated account editing, posting, or built-in Twitter analytics.
VoiceMOAT tool support requires a separate connection and a Pro or Enterprise plan, according to the skill.

use_cases.title: Clarify a professional profile
use_cases.description: Replace a job-title-focused bio with a clear explanation of the topics you share and why readers should follow.

use_cases.title: Align a founder profile with current work
use_cases.description: Review the name, bio, and pinned tweet after an offer changes, without replacing profile elements that still work.

use_cases.title: Connect profile copy to regular posts
use_cases.description: Compare profile promises with recent writing and choose a representative pinned tweet for visitors arriving from replies or timeline posts.

prompt_templates.title: Review a bio
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Twitter bio: [bio]. I post about [topics] for [audience]. Suggest a clearer version and explain what to keep.

prompt_templates.title: Review the full profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my name [name], bio [bio], pinned tweet [tweet], and attached profile images. Visitors usually arrive from [source]. Prioritize changes and identify what works.

prompt_templates.title: Update a profile after a role change
prompt_templates.prompt: My role changed from [old role] to [new role]. Review this profile [details] against these recent posts [posts]. Recommend focused edits without keyword stuffing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: align profile copy with a new role and existing writing.

prompt_templates.title: Check voice consistency with VoiceMOAT
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this profile [details] and recent posts [posts]. Use connected VoiceMOAT tools, if available, to check topics and bio voice. Otherwise, use only supplied material.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review voice consistency with optional connector support.

output_examples.input: Name: Maya. Bio: Product manager, reader, coffee fan. Posts: practical onboarding lessons for product teams.
output: Suggested bio: Practical onboarding lessons for product teams, with examples from the products I work on.
Keep your personal name. Replace the generic interests with a clear reason to follow.

output_examples.input: An independent developer shares debugging walkthroughs but pins an old event announcement. The avatar is clear; the header has tiny text.
output: Replace the event announcement with a debugging walkthrough that represents your current posts.
Remove or enlarge the header text so it remains readable on a phone.
Keep any bio wording that already explains the debugging topics you cover.

best_practices: Provide your current profile, recent posts, and the main source of profile visits.
Describe what followers receive using topics and examples you actually share.
Review recommended edits at mobile size and preserve elements that already communicate clearly.
anti_patterns: Treating a bio rewrite as a guaranteed way to gain followers.
Replacing every profile element without checking what already works.
Filling the name and bio with keywords, credentials, or unrelated interests.

faq.question: What should I provide for a profile review?
faq.answer: Share your name field, bio, pinned tweet, recent posts, and profile images. Include how visitors usually find your account.

faq.question: Will this skill edit my Twitter account directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and suggested copy. The skill does not include account editing or posting automation.

faq.question: Does it guarantee more followers?
faq.answer: No. It helps clarify your profile for existing visitors. It does not create visits or promise follower growth.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. Profile review can use supplied material. Connected VoiceMOAT tools add voice insights and consistency checks when available.

faq.question: What does the VoiceMOAT connection require?
faq.answer: The skill states that the connector requires a Pro or Enterprise plan. It also lists free web tools that need no account.

faq.question: Can it review my avatar and header?
faq.answer: Yes, when images are available. It checks readability at timeline and mobile sizes rather than only inspecting full-size uploads.
